judged_text: The migration defaults posts.cook_method to 1, which is :raw_html in Post.cook_methods (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns regular=0, raw_html=1), so every existing post and every newly created post without an explicit cook_method is silently reclassified as raw HTML. Post#cook returns `raw` whenever cook_method == raw_html (app/models/post.rb:131-133), so after this migration every pre-existing post renders its uncooked markdown source as its cooked HTML, and all new posts created via the normal PostCreator path (which never sets cook_method) inherit the DB default of 1 and are likewise rendered raw. The author's own spec (topic_embed_spec.rb) proves the value mapping: posts created with cook_method raw_html assert `post.cooked.should == post.raw`. This is a silent reclassification of the entire posts table on deploy; the correct default for the new column is 0 (:regular).

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on an assumed Enum mapping (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) => regular=0, raw_html=1). That mapping is not shown anywhere in the diff, so the claim that the DB default of 1 corresponds to :raw_html is not verifiable from the PR. In fact, the diff itself strongly suggests a 1-based enum convention: the code already uses Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action) for Post.types, and the new migration sets cook_method default: 1 (which would be an odd choice if 1 meant the *second* enum value). The added spec only asserts equality to Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] and that raw_html posts have cooked==raw; it does not prove raw_html maps to 1. Therefore the “silent reclassification of the entire posts table” conclusion is unsupported by the diff.
